assumptions: MaxEnt is Yeo and Burge's published model with their trained tables.
Typicality is log-odds against base frequencies measured at TAIR10's annotated sites, so it speaks for a plant host.
limits: No verdict and no threshold: neither model publishes a cutoff, so it ranks and the call is yours.
The two numbers are on different scales and are never combined.
The Arabidopsis matrices have no upstream to grade them: the claim is that re-running their generator against Ensembl Plants 63 reproduces them exactly.
bio.jane/contract.noReading: The ranked splice sites with their MaxEnt bits; the Optimize panel lists them against the annotated introns and writes no sentence over them. The optimizer's reading is on optimize_sequence.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which splice donors and acceptors does this sequence spell, by maximum-entropy strength and by typicality against measured Arabidopsis sites?

description: Find the splice sites a sequence accidentally spells - the check a codon-optimised CDS needs before it goes into a plant or any other eukaryotic host, because a synonymous swap chosen for codon usage or GC can spell a donor or acceptor that was not there before, and the transcript is then spliced somewhere nobody intended. Every GT and AG is scored two ways that are NOT on one scale and are never combined: `maxEnt` is strength under Yeo & Burge's published maximum-entropy model, and `typicality` is log-odds against base frequencies MEASURED at the annotated splice sites of Arabidopsis thaliana TAIR10 (Ensembl Plants 63). IT RETURNS NO VERDICT and has no default threshold: neither model publishes a cutoff, so this RANKS candidates and what counts as dangerous is your call, with both numbers in front of you.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

max_results.description: how many to return, strongest first. Advanced.

min_maxent.description: report only sites at or above this MaxEntScan score, in bits. UNSET BY DEFAULT and deliberately so - MaxEntScan publishes no significance cutoff and the measured matrices are a description rather than a classifier, so a default here would be a decision boundary nobody has published. Set it when you have a threshold of your own. In bits.

sequence.description: the DNA to scan - leave unset to use the open record.

strand.description: which strand to read. Both by default: an antisense site still splices a transcript made from the other strand, and in a construct both may be transcribed. Name the gene's own strand when you know it, and the other strand's candidates stop crowding the ranking.

name: scan_splice_sites

sites.description: the candidates, strongest MaxEnt first, each with its kind, position on the strand you passed, the window that was scored, and both scores

strongest.description: the highest-scoring candidate, or null when the sequence is too short to hold a window

strongestMaxEnt.description: that candidate's MaxEntScan score on its own, for a comparison downstream, or null when there is no candidate: 0 is a real MaxEntScan score
